gen-gf-gfs-didot-fs-bespoke-sans: Sharp and refined, Bespoke Sans leaves generous gaps where its curves meet the stem. GFS Didot sits above it with a hint of pen pressure in every curve, a bookish voice next to a crisp one.
gen-gf-gfs-neohellenic-fs-literata: GFS Neohellenic sets round, solid-looking words with a steady line and a clearly open e, never a flicker of pressure. Literata below feels bookish and settled.
gen-gf-gidugu-fs-literata: Literata reads sophisticated and bookish, its curved letters leaving wide mouths where they could have closed. Yet Gidugu above bends its end strokes in almost shut, so the two make a neat opposition.
gen-gf-gilda-display-fs-bespoke-sans: Traditional and editorial, Gilda Display lets hairline strokes sit beside heavy ink. Bespoke Sans underneath stays sharp and low in contrast, with generous space around its curve ends, so the heading's drama never has to compete.
gen-gf-gloock-fs-bespoke-sans: Bespoke Sans is sharp and refined, with generous space between its curve ends and the stem. Bespoke Sans also lets Gloock's chiseled thick stems and scalpel-thin curves carry all the authority.
gen-gf-glory-fs-literata: Glory's pen-lifted curves leave every loop unfinished. Literata follows with a soft cadence of fuller stems and slimmer links, so a long page feels bookish and unhurried.
gen-gf-google-sans-fs-literata: Marker-plain and friendly, Google Sans gives every stroke a pipe-like body. Literata answers with sturdy bowls and lightly thinned links, and that mix of plain and bookish is the pair's best quality.
gen-gf-google-sans-flex-fs-literata: Google Sans Flex looks like bent paperclip wire, with a gaping c that shows at any size. And Literata carries a longer read gently, its bowls thinning slightly at the sides with a sophisticated, bookish ease.
gen-gf-gothic-a1-fs-literata: Literata reads sophisticated and bookish, its strokes moderately modulated and its curves open. But Gothic A1 earns its place big and brief, where its wide ring of a c can be seen.
gen-gf-gotu-fs-literata: Literata brings a sophisticated, bookish text serif, with sturdy thin lines and slightly heavier thick ones. Gotu steps in above it, approachable and modest in its curves.
